# Real-world corpus

Drop real `.xlsx` / `.xlsm` files here. They are used by `test/corpus.test.ts`
and by `scripts/validate-corpus.mjs` to check that `sheet-lite` behaves on
files we did **not** generate ourselves.

## Why this exists

Fixtures generated by code (ours or ExcelJS) are "well-behaved". Real files —
exported from Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice, ERPs, invoices, reports — are
messy, and that is where bugs hide (the "long tail"). This folder is how the
promise *"open, edit and don't break your file"* gets tested against reality.

## How to add files

1. Copy your file in, e.g. `invoice-2019.xlsx`, `erp-export.xlsm`.
2. Keep the name descriptive; spaces are fine.
3. Prefer files **under ~2 MB** (they are committed to the repo). For bigger
   ones, tell me and we can keep them local instead.

Nothing else is required. The tests discover every `*.xlsx` / `*.xlsm` here.

## What is checked for each file

- It **opens** and every sheet/row/cell is readable without throwing.
- If it is unsupported (zip64, encrypted, data descriptors) it must fail with a
  **coded `SheetLiteError`** — a clean rejection, never a crash or corrupt output.
- A **no-op round-trip** returns the original bytes verbatim.
- A **single-cell edit** leaves every other part **byte-for-byte identical**.
- (When LibreOffice is available) the edited file **re-opens without repair**.

## Licence / privacy

Only add files you are allowed to share. No personal or confidential data:
redact it or use a synthetic stand-in. If in doubt, keep the file out of git and
run the validator locally.

## Run it

```sh
pnpm build && node scripts/validate-corpus.mjs   # detailed report
pnpm test                                        # runs the corpus test too
```
